newsitem.title: CHINA: HK GOLD CLOSES SLIGHTLY FIRMER IN QUIET TRADE.
newsitem.headline: HK GOLD CLOSES SLIGHTLY FIRMER IN QUIET TRADE.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed slightly firmer on Thursday after trading within a 40 U.S. cents range all day in an extremely quiet session, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$318.70/319.20 an ounce against New York's US$318.30/80 close on Wednesday and Hong Kong's previous close of US$318.50/319.00.
"The local market has been very quiet, with a small amount of short-covering interest," said a dealer at an international metals house.
Physical gold demand had been steady, but had slowed after gold prices bounced back from lows near $317 per ounce to $319 per ounce.
Local gold ended HK$1 lower at HK$2,956 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged at nil on Thursday.
